method: Define possible viewer needs and falsifiable outcomes in pre-existing YouTube content categories, using dated platform activity only as a topic rationale. No tested niche demand, business promise, demographic persuasion, pilot spending or content publication.
population: No recruited experimental sample; proposals may only become studies after permissible aggregate data access and a fixed hypothesis, comparator, exposure and observation window

hypotheses.hypothesis: Some viewers seeking event-specific makeup techniques may prefer a stepwise instructional video to an otherwise matched inspirational clip.
hypotheses.viewer_need: Practice a particular look with clear product/technique steps before a seasonal event.
hypotheses.negative_result_rule: No favorable matched owner Search impression-to-view response under a preregistered confidence or minimum-exposure rule; do not call this a zero demand result.
hypotheses.limitations: Over one billion historical title-subset view events do not count unique prospective tutorial customers or establish 2026 pilot demand.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A source-linked explainer of a stable topic might attract sustained YouTube Search visits beyond its initial release window compared with an event-recap video matched for topic and channel age.
hypotheses.viewer_need: Receive a verifiable, retrievable explanation with public source references.
hypotheses.negative_result_rule: No sustained repeat Search-origin viewing in preregistered age-matched later windows after sufficient comparable exposure; results may be censored.
hypotheses.limitations: YouTube's 2024 broad video-essay view events cannot establish actual source-linked search demand, labor or hourly earnings.

hypotheses.hypothesis: For a defined opt-in adult podcast consumer sample, an audiovisual episode may address a complementary viewing need relative to the audio-only version without producing a larger unique audience.
hypotheses.viewer_need: Choose whether to watch or listen to a discussion, depending on context and device.
hypotheses.negative_result_rule: No measurable format-choice difference in the defined adult opt-in sample under a preregistered analysis plan; cannot infer missing total audience.
hypotheses.limitations: Edison's 82% video and 78% audio-only US weekly consumer responses overlap and were not a YouTube-specific experiment.

prespecification_gates: Record niche inclusion predicate independently of the video performance outcome.
Define a comparison audience, video format, source of traffic, region/language and like-age window.
Require channel authorization or explicit consent for private analytics; do not retrieve identifiable individuals.
Choose the primary event-level metric, sample denominator and stop rules before observing results.
Include unpublished attempts, zero-view entries, production hours, permissions, refund/rights costs and duplicate revenues.
Fix maximum new cash and creator-labor ceilings in advance; no project may spend without explicit authorization.
Do not turn title-filtered public topic views or podcast survey response percentages into observed price, conversion or creator-income forecasts.
Prefer documented inconclusive outcomes to invented niche rankings or causal claims.
